lens: citations/build/gates (pointers resolve, prior rulings actually say what's claimed)
central_claim: A census (enumerate-then-grade) of 217 cancer-treatment modality classes finds 112 (18 live) never pointed at by any prior search here, closes 84 of them, and registers 31 surviving classes as routes -- with every prior ruling accounted for by a pointer rather than restated.

blockers.summary: The Sec.2 headline verdict-count table and the Sec.3 opening line ('Thirty-one classes survive') are stale RIGHT NOW against the canonical registry the document names as its own source of truth. The registry currently holds 20 `candidate` rows and 95 `excluded` rows, not 31 and 84; the generated view the document points readers to for 'the full register' states the same 20/95 split explicitly.
blockers.evidence: Doc Sec.2 table: '✕ `excluded` | 84 | 83' and '⭑ `candidate` | 31 | 9'. Doc Sec.3: 'Thirty-one classes survive. They group into seven themes...'. Actual systems/graph/modalities.json at this commit: Counter({'excluded': 95, ... 'candidate': 20, ...}) (verified by direct load: 217 rows, verdicts sum to 217). systems/views/modality-census.md at the same commit (the document's own linked 'full register') states verbatim: '| ⭑ `candidate` | 20 | 6 |' and '| ✕ `excluded` | 95 | 86 |', with the file's own summary line reading '⭑ 111 classes no prior search here had pointed at ... 14 of the 111 are live'. The doc's own corrected headline (Sec.2, after the 127->112 correction) still says '112 of 217 classes had never been pointed at ... and 18 of those are live' -- both numbers (112, 18) diverge from the registry/view's current 111 and 14. This is not a case the document flags as superseded (unlike the 127->112 correction it does perform); the drift is silent and un-reconciled. The 11-row swing between candidate(31->20) and excluded(84->95) is explained by concrete named classes the document itself discusses as still-live in Sec.3.1/3.3 (Transcriptional CDK inhibition, ALK/ROS1) that the registry has already re-graded to `excluded` on 2026-08-09 -- the same date as this document -- via the very artifact (census-route-expression-grading.json) the document cites elsewhere for a *different* six classes: RT-TXN-CDK verdict 'SUPPORTED -- the most concordant elevation in the census, on both platforms' / route_action 'down-grade: supported on abundance, closed on the axis that matters'; RT-ALK-HIT verdict 'UNATTRIBUTABLE BY EXPRESSION' / route_action 'demote and fold into the kinase paper as a corrected reading of a lead'. Neither of these gradings, nor their closure, is mentioned in Sec.3.1 ('never assessed against any EMC data, and never given one') or Sec.3.3 ('the first step separates the observation from the hypothesis') -- both sections present these classes as still awaiting their first assessment when the document's own cited grading artifact and the canonical registry already closed them the same day.
blockers.fix: Regenerate or re-read systems/views/modality-census.md and reconcile every count in Sec.2 (the verdict table, the never-searched total/live-count, the band table) against it; add a Sec.2.1-style correction note (the document already has the pattern) rather than leaving the drift silent. In Sec.3.1 and 3.3, either report the RT-TXN-CDK/RT-ALK-HIT expression-grading verdicts (as Sec.3.2a/3.8 do for the other routes graded that day) or explain why those two are being treated differently from the routes that got the correction treatment.

blockers.summary: Self-contained internal inconsistency, checkable without any external file: Sec.5 says 'Thirty-one rows carry `already_rejected`' while the document's own Sec.2 table states already_rejected = 33 (and the registry confirms 33).
blockers.evidence: Doc Sec.2 table row: '✕ `already_rejected` -- a prior document settled it | 33 | 0'. Doc Sec.5: 'Thirty-one rows carry `already_rejected` with a resolvable pointer into the owning document.' systems/graph/modalities.json: Counter of verdict=='already_rejected' is 33 (all with `prior_coverage: searched_before`, matching the '0 never searched' cell). A second, smaller self-contained arithmetic slip in the same Sec.2 band table: the `drug_mechanism` row reads '162 | 87 | 53 %', but 87/162 = 53.7%, which rounds to 54%, not 53% -- the 53% figure is only consistent with the registry's true count of 86 (86/162 = 53.1%), meaning the 87 in that cell does not match its own adjacent percentage.
blockers.fix: Change Sec.5's 'Thirty-one' to 'Thirty-three' (or regenerate the sentence from the registry). Fix the drug_mechanism band row to 86 (matching its own stated 53%) rather than 87.

blockers.summary: RET's disposition is reported inconsistently between the document's own two cited sources of truth, and the document never surfaces or reconciles the conflict. Sec.3.8, sourced to census-route-expression-grading.json, reports RET as still open ('does not close the lane', moved from 'activated' to 'expressed'); the canonical registry row for the same class is verdict=`excluded`, closed on completely unrelated grounds.
blockers.evidence: Doc Sec.3.8 table: 'RET | split -- the receptor holds; the module that switches it on is depleted on both platforms' and the accompanying text: 'That does not close the lane... it moves the claim the lane may make from activated to expressed.' This text is a faithful restatement of research/modalities/census-route-expression-grading.json -> routes.RT-RET: verdict 'SPLIT — receptor supported, ligand-dependent activation route weakened.', route_action 'keep, with the co-receptor reading carried as a stated caveat'. But systems/graph/modalities.json -> MOD-RET (the row this document's own scope statement says owns the verdict: 'it does not own the census rows, which live in systems/graph/modalities.json') states verdict: 'excluded', with rationale: '⛔ RE-GRADED 2026-08-09 on EVIDENCE QUALITY and on ELIGIBILITY, not on a negative measurement. ... Reading the source shows the activation claim is a single sentence in a paywalled abstract, about a limited set of at most ten tumours, with no recoverable denominator and no assay attribution -- and the approved selective agents are approved on a molecular state this disease is not reported to be in.' -- a completely different closure reason (evidence quality of the original activation report) than the co-receptor/ligand expression finding the manuscript reports, dated the same day. The manuscript's narrative reflects the superseded 'keep' verdict from the expression-grading artifact and never mentions the registry's later, contradictory 'excluded' disposition.
blockers.fix: Re-read systems/graph/modalities.json -> MOD-RET and either update Sec.3.8's RET row/text to reflect the actual current registry disposition (excluded, on evidence-quality grounds) or, if the evidence-quality closure is itself wrong/premature, flag that as an open conflict between two committed artifacts rather than silently reporting only the friendlier one.

blockers.summary: 'Only the 23 candidate rows were adjudicated' (Sec.2.1) is not supported by the artifact it cites. census-novelty-audit.json records exactly 20 rows with verdict=='candidate' (not 23), and every one of its 73 flagged rows -- with no exception -- carries adjudication:'UNREVIEWED -- a term match is not a coverage claim'.
blockers.evidence: Doc Sec.2.1: '⚠ It flagged 73 rows and only the 23 candidate rows were adjudicated, because those are the ones anyone would act on.' research/modalities/census-novelty-audit.json at this commit: n_rows_with_a_candidate_collision = 73 (matches '73 rows', good); direct enumeration of the `findings` dict's 73 entries shows exactly 20 with `verdict`=='candidate', and a Counter over every entry's `adjudication` field returns a single value across all 73: 'UNREVIEWED — a term match is not a coverage claim' -- there is no field distinguishing 'adjudicated' from 'not adjudicated', and nothing in the artifact records that any subset (23 or otherwise) received a different disposition.
blockers.fix: Either correct '23' to '20' (the count actually present with verdict=='candidate' in the audit artifact) and point to whatever artifact/commit actually recorded the adjudication (since census-novelty-audit.json itself shows none), or add the missing evidence to census-novelty-audit.json so the claim is checkable from the cited source.

blockers.summary: Sec.2.1's explicit 8-item enumeration of 'the incumbent arsenal' does not match the registry's actual 8 `in_clinical_use` rows: it names 'a minor-groove binder' (which the registry classifies as `on_board`, not `in_clinical_use`) and omits the registry's real 8th in-clinical-use row, 'Observation and deferred intervention'.
blockers.evidence: Doc Sec.2.1: 'the incumbent arsenal is 8 classes ... multi-kinase antiangiogenic inhibitors, anthracyclines, alkylators, a minor-groove binder, a KIT inhibitor used once under a biomarker restriction, interferon in case reports, radiotherapy, and surgery.' systems/graph/modalities.json filtered to verdict=='in_clinical_use' returns exactly 8 rows: MOD-ANTHRACYCLINE, MOD-ALKYLATOR, MOD-VEGFR-TKI, MOD-KIT-PDGFR, MOD-INTERFERON, MOD-EBRT, MOD-SURGERY, MOD-WATCHFUL-WAITING (Observation and deferred intervention) -- no minor-groove binder among them. The class the manuscript is presumably naming, MOD-DNA-MINOR-GROOVE ('DNA minor-groove binders / fusion-TF displacers'), exists in the registry but with verdict `on_board` (an already-covered route, not an incumbent-clinical-use class) -- a materially different category under this document's own taxonomy.
blockers.fix: Replace 'a minor-groove binder' with 'observation and deferred intervention' (or the correct label for MOD-WATCHFUL-WAITING) in the Sec.2.1 sentence, matching the registry's actual 8 `in_clinical_use` rows.

p1s.summary: The strategy_and_architecture band row's percentage (28%) is a floor of 4/14=28.57%, which most readers would round to 29% -- not itself wrong given an unstated floor convention, but worth a footnote on rounding method since the sibling drug_mechanism row's percentage is currently inconsistent with its own count (see Blocker 2) and a stated convention would make both auditable.
p1s.fix: State the rounding convention once (e.g. 'floor') so every percentage in the table is mechanically reproducible from its two neighboring integers.
